newsitem.title: PERU: U.S., Mexico firms eye Peru's La Oroya complex.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Mexico firms eye Peru's La Oroya complex.

text.p: The Doe Run Co of the United States and Mexico's Industrias Penoles S.A. are interested in acquiring Peru's hard-to-privatize La Oroya smelting and refining complex, an official said Monday.
"They have visited the complex and I believe they are strongly interested," said Enrique Olivares, chief spokesman for state mining giant Empresa Minera del Centro del Peru (Centromin).
The government has set an April 14 auction for its third attempt to privatize Centromin's most important asset, Empresa Metalurgica La Oroya S.A.
The complex was not sold in its first two attempts at privatization due to ennvironmental problems, officials said.

"The Doe Run Company and Penoles also have had access to Centromin's data room and several companies have requested bid specifications for the auction but we have only given them to those which meet the basic requirements," Olivares said.
He said that La Oroya's sale will be done under a scheme known as "capitalization," in which bidders will offer a per- share price as well as a percentage capital increase.

"It's an interesting (sale) model," Olivares said. "Each bidder will have to present its capital increase offer keeping in mind a minimum of 51 percent participation that will allow it control of the company."
The La Oroya complex, located in Peru's central Andes 190 kms east of Lima at an altitude of 3,700 meters (yards) above sea level, processes 22 metals and their subproducts.
The last privatization of a Centromin asset was in December, when Brazil's Paranapanema offered to pay $12.7 million and invest $100 million over five years in the Yauliyacu polymetal deposit.
Yauliyacu is due to be transferred to Paranapanema on Tuesday.
